19 A box of mass 4.9 kg is pushed at a constant velocity from point P at the bottom of an inclined
plane to point Q at the top.
The box is pushed by a force of 64 N acting parallel to the slope.
The slope is inclined at an angle of 20° to the horizontal and the box moves through a vertical
height of 5.8 m.
Q
64 N
5.8 m
P
20°
What is the work done against the frictional force acting on the block between P and Q?
A
280 J
B
810 J
C
960 J
D
1100 J

hints: Notice the box moves at constant velocity up the $20^{\circ}$ slope through a vertical height of $5.8 \text{ m}$ while pushed by $64 \text{ N}$ parallel to the slope.
Use energy conservation for constant kinetic energy: work by $64 \text{ N}$ along the slope = gain in $mgh$ + work against friction.
First find the slope distance from $\sin 20^{\circ} = 5.8/d$, then calculate $64d$ and $4.9 \times 9.81 \times 5.8$ and subtract.
walkthrough: Find the distance moved along the slope from the right-angled triangle in the diagram. With vertical height $h = 5.8 \text{ m}$ and angle $20^{\circ}$, $\sin 20^{\circ} = h/d$, so $d = 5.8/\sin 20^{\circ} \approx 17.0 \text{ m}$.
Calculate the total work supplied by the pushing force parallel to displacement: $W_{in} = Fd = 64 \times 17.0 \approx 1085 \text{ J}$.
Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained: $E_p = mgh = 4.9 \times 9.81 \times 5.8 \approx 279 \text{ J}$.
Because velocity is constant, kinetic energy does not change, so the input work is split into stored potential energy plus work against friction: $W_{in} = E_p + W_{friction}$.
Subtract to isolate friction: $W_{friction} = 1085 - 279 \approx 806 \text{ J}$, about $810 \text{ J}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the gain in gravitational potential energy $mgh$ about $280 \text{ J}$, not the work left over to overcome friction.

B.explanation: Total work in minus $mgh$ leaves about $1085 - 279 \approx 810 \text{ J}$ done against friction.

C.explanation: This is too large because it subtracts too little potential energy from the work done by the $64 \text{ N}$ push.

D.explanation: This is the total work done by the $64 \text{ N}$ force along the slope, about $1100 \text{ J}$, before subtracting the $mgh$ stored as potential energy.
